venue.name: Parksville Museum
venue.description: The Parksville Museum is a heritage park on East Island Highway run by the Parksville and District Historical Society, which began in 1976 after local residents saved the Knox Church from demolition. Eight heritage buildings stand on the grounds, some dating back to 1885, among them the church, the Montrose School, a fire hall, two post offices and Craig's Cottage, alongside a blacksmith forge, a tractor barn, a canoe shelter, an exhibit hall, a nature trail and the Marion Craig Courtyard. It is open Thursday to Monday from 11 am to 5 pm, closed on BC statutory holidays, and admission is by donation with $5 a person suggested. The archives hold more than 6,000 historical photographs and are run by volunteer archivists, and nothing on the site describes a school program, a guided tour or a group rate.
venue.address: 1245 East Island Highway, Parksville, BC V9P 2E5

facility_notes.washrooms: Access to nearby outdoor washrooms from the Marion Craig Courtyard. Two further washrooms are staff ones inside the main Exhibition Hall and are only opened for people hiring a room.
facility_notes.lunch_space: Our stunning courtyard is open year-round for you to enjoy. Spend some time, have a coffee, a picnic, or just relax outdoors.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: The Knox Heritage Church is fully wheelchair accessible and the Heritage Room is wheelchair accessible. Nothing is said about the older heritage buildings or the nature trail.

venue.hours_notes: Open Thursday through Monday, 11 am to 5 pm, and closed on BC statutory holidays. Outside those hours a paid booking of the grounds takes precedence over general use.
venue.seasonal_notes: The Marion Craig Courtyard is open year round. The Second Sundays Artisan Market runs on the second Sunday of each month from May through September, and 13 September 2026 is the last one listed. The events page also still carries listings from earlier years, including a Friday evening market series from 2023, so the dates need reading carefully.
venue.price_year_or_season: The suggested $5 donation was read from the live contact page on 10 September 2026 and carries no year. Their room hire rate sheets are headed 2026.

programs.name: Self guided visit to the museum grounds
programs.description: The museum is a heritage park you walk around yourself. Eight heritage buildings are on the grounds, among them the Montrose School, the fire hall, the French Creek and Craig's Crossing post offices, McMillan House, Craig's Cottage, Craig's Cabin and the Knox Church, and there is a working blacksmith forge with the only traditional Japanese forge in Western Canada, an interactive exhibit about the E and N Railway inside Craig's Cabin, the Mosaic Pavilion on Vancouver Island forestry and logging, a tractor barn, a canoe shelter, an exhibit hall and a short nature trail. Self guided tour boards are set out around the Marion Craig Courtyard, which is open year round. Admission is by donation and the museum suggests $5 a person. No guided tour, school program, group rate, group size limit, notice period or way of booking a group is published anywhere on the site.
programs.what_children_do: Walk between the old buildings and go inside them, look round the schoolhouse, the fire hall and the post offices, try the hands on parts of the railway and forestry exhibits, see the blacksmith forge, read the boards around the courtyard and walk the short nature trail.
programs.our_note: There is nobody to lead the visit, so read the boards yourself and decide in advance which buildings you want. They open at 11 and close at 5 and they are shut on Tuesdays and Wednesdays, which rules out a lot of mornings. Admission is by donation with $5 a head suggested, so agree what the group is giving before you arrive rather than at the gate.
programs.practical_summary: There are outdoor washrooms near the courtyard, and the courtyard itself is open all year and is where a picnic would happen. The church and the meeting room take a wheelchair, but nothing is said about the older buildings, the nature trail, shelter in the rain, or where a bus would park, so it is worth a call.
programs.evidence: Visit our museum and uncover historic Parksville through our many hands-on, engaging exhibits.

gaps: NO SCHOOL OR GROUP OFFERING IS PUBLISHED. There is no school program page, no guided tour, no group rate, no group size limit, no notice period and no way to book a group. Their own sitemap lists ten pages and not one of them mentions schools, teachers, daycares, field trips or group visits. Whether they would take a booked class at all is a phone call.

Admission is by donation with $5 a person suggested, which is neither free nor a price, so nothing has been recorded as a cost. For a group of 25 the suggestion would come to $125. That is arithmetic on their suggestion, not a group rate they have quoted, so agree the amount with them before you go.
Youngest age welcomed is not stated, and no age or grade range is published for anything on the site.
How long a visit takes is not stated.

Bus parking is not mentioned. The only parking note anywhere on the site is written for their Sunday market and points people to street parking along NW Bay Road, Franklin's Gull Road and beside Serious Coffee, which is not a plan for a coach.

Whether there is anywhere to shelter or eat indoors if it rains is not stated for an ordinary visitor. Their room hire guide says a courtyard booking caught by rain can move into the church for up to 75 people or the meeting room for up to 35, but that is written for people paying to hire the space.

Wheelchair access is only addressed for the Knox Church and the Heritage Room, both of which are rentable spaces. Nothing is said about the older heritage buildings, the paths or the nature trail. Stroller access is not mentioned at all.

The events page still carries listings from past years alongside the current ones, including a Friday evening market that ran September to October 2023. The 2026 items that are still ahead are the Second Sundays market on 13 September and a Storyteller Series concert on 27 September at $25 a ticket, which is an adult evening event rather than anything for a group of children.
The archival services page lists five services but the fee table beside them did not load in either a plain fetch or a browser, so the archive fees are not recorded here.

The photograph used as the header is the same one the site uses for social sharing, but that copy is served over plain http, so the version from their home page was recorded instead. Their own alt text for it is thin but it is theirs, so it has been kept as written rather than replaced.

Their address link carries a Google Maps place pin, and the coordinates here come from the pin at the end of that link rather than from the map centre earlier in the same link. Geocoding the street address independently landed about 20 metres away, which is a good match.

values: Spend some time - have a coffee, a picnic, or just relax outdoors
No food or drink is permitted on site unless it is provided by a food-safe kitchen or a licensed food vendor with Health Authority approval
conflicts.note: Their pages say two different things about food. The exhibits page invites you to bring a picnic into the courtyard, while their room hire guide says no food or drink is allowed on site unless it comes from a food safe kitchen or a licensed vendor. The stricter rule may only apply to people paying to hire the space, but packed lunches for a group are worth clearing on the phone before you go.
